studies.title: Orangefarbenes Deckblatt
studies.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Create one outstanding graphic concept for an UNOFFICIAL Rudolstadt Festival companion app. This is an exploration of the folded festival plan motif, NOT a finished app icon. The user rejected crude polygons, generic fonts, awkward perspective and cheap clipart. Aim for a distinctive, beautifully proportioned editorial symbol, designed by an experienced brand designer.
References: Image 1 supplies the distinctive original condensed lowercase lettering, stacked "rudol" then "stadt"; preserve its letter shapes and the complete spelling (r u d o l / s t a d t). Image 2 supplies the official festival's orange and rhythm of rotated little squares, inspiration rather than a full official logo lockup. Use plum purple, vivid burnt orange and warm ivory only. Keep faces solid flat colors, precise clean edges, no textures, grain, outlines, rendered material, glass, bevels, reflections, lighting gradients or drop shadows. Fold depth comes entirely from shape, negative space and contrasting solid faces. One isolated generously sized motif on genuinely transparent background, no tile, no rounded-square app background, no labels or explanatory text. The shape must remain compelling at small sizes. Exact allowed text: "rudol" above "stadt", no other text. Do not paste a rectangular logo block over the drawing: integrate it deliberately into the main cover with excellent spacing. The logo reference has transparent negative space, not a black rectangle.
Direction: a beautiful partially unfolded pocket festival plan. A single dominant orange front cover with ivory original lettering, a little turned counterclockwise, and two ivory/plum folds opening compactly to the upper right. The whole silhouette is tightly composed, almost square and slightly lively, never a wide brochure. A carefully drawn single plum river on the exposed ivory map face has a distinctive gentle bend; three tiny rotated orange square venue marks alongside it echo the festival brand. No generic meandering line with dots and no map pin. Two or three generous panels, not many tiny details. Preserve a convincingly connected folded sheet, consistent edge geometry, understated fold seams, subtly softened real paper corners through silhouette only. The orange cover is roughly 60 percent of the motif; visible map 40 percent. Striking asymmetric balance and clean empty areas.
